# CANDIDATE: TREND_STRENGTH_FILTER_FOR_BEAR_PUTS

**Filed:** 2026-07-21
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** filter_change
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

We hypothesize that bear put entries on days with weak intraday downward trend strength (shallow slope) are more likely to be losers or have reduced profit. By requiring a sufficiently steep downward trend (slope more negative than a threshold) at the time of entry, we can filter out weak-trend entries that tend to lose money or underperform, thereby increasing edge_capture on J anchor days by reducing losses on losing days and/or increasing profits on winner days.

## Mechanism

In addition to the existing BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON context filters, we add a requirement that the 5m descending trendline slope (computed over the last 20 bars) must be less than -0.01 (i.e., declining at least 1 point per 100 bars) at the trigger bar. This is computed using the same market_structure.py logic as the existing structure veto but extended to capture slope magnitude. If the slope is >= -0.01 (too flat or upward), the entry is blocked.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline (based on BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON position sizing)
2. **Sample bias:** We propose to test on the full 16-month OPRA dataset (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) with a walk-forward OOS window of the last 4 months (2026-02-19 to 2026-06-18) to avoid look-ahead bias. Overfit risk is medium as we are adding a single parameter (slope threshold) that will be optimized on IS data.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (will be run as part of Stage-1 backtest via grinder)
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (will be validated on top 3 J days as part of OP-20 disclosure 4)
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: if the filter blocks a winner day, edge_capture could decrease significantly.
   - Max drawdown: could increase if the filter causes us to miss winners and take more losers.
   - Blow-up scenario: if the slope threshold is too tight, we may take too few trades and suffer from sampling error.
